import re

def parse(lines):
    pkg = {}
    pl = []
    pdoc = [[]]
    rows = []
    rl = []
    skip = []
    section = ''
    cur = None
    blank = False
    decl_re = re.compile(r'^(func|type|const|var)\b')
    func_re = re.compile(r'^func\s+(?:\((?P<recv>[^)]*)\)\s*)?(?P<name>\w+)')
    other_re = re.compile(r'^(?:type|const|var)\s+(?P<name>\w+)')
    n = len(lines)
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        s = lines[i]
        if not s.strip():
            blank = True
            i += 1
            continue
        m = re.match(r'^package\s+(\S+)(?:\s*//\s*import\s+"([^"]*)")?', s)
        if m and 'package' not in pkg and not rows:
            pkg['package'] = m.group(1)
            pkg['import'] = m.group(2) or ''
            pl.append(i)
            blank = False
            i += 1
            continue
        if not s[0].isspace() and re.match(r'^[A-Z][A-Z ]*[A-Z]$', s.strip()):
            section = s.strip()
            skip.append(i)
            cur = None
            blank = False
            i += 1
            continue
        dm = decl_re.match(s)
        if dm:
            decl = [s.rstrip()]
            idxs = [i]
            if s.rstrip().endswith(('{', '(')):
                j = i + 1
                while j < n:
                    decl.append(lines[j].rstrip())
                    idxs.append(j)
                    if lines[j].startswith(('}', ')')):
                        break
                    j += 1
                i = j
            recv = ''
            name = ''
            fm = func_re.match(s)
            if dm.group(1) == 'func' and fm:
                name = fm.group('name')
                if fm.group('recv'):
                    recv = fm.group('recv').split()[-1]
            else:
                om = other_re.match(s)
                if om:
                    name = om.group('name')
            cur = {'section': section, 'kind': dm.group(1), 'receiver': recv, 'name': name, 'declaration': '\n'.join(decl), 'doc': [[]]}
            rows.append(cur)
            rl.extend(idxs)
            blank = False
            i += 1
            continue
        if cur is not None:
            if blank and cur['doc'][-1]:
                cur['doc'].append([])
            cur['doc'][-1].append(s.strip())
            rl.append(i)
        else:
            if blank and pdoc[-1]:
                pdoc.append([])
            pdoc[-1].append(s.strip())
            pl.append(i)
        blank = False
        i += 1
    for r in rows:
        r['doc'] = '\n\n'.join(' '.join(p) for p in r['doc'] if p)
    blocks = []
    if pl:
        pkg['doc'] = '\n\n'.join(' '.join(p) for p in pdoc if p)
        blocks.append({'name': 'package', 'kind': 'kv', 'lines': pl, 'records': [pkg]})
    if rows:
        blocks.append({'name': 'declarations', 'kind': 'table', 'lines': sorted(rl), 'records': rows})
    return {'blocks': blocks, 'skip': skip}

package ring // import "container/ring"

Package ring implements operations on circular lists.

TYPES

type Ring struct {
	Value any // for use by client; untouched by this library
	// Has unexported fields.
}
    A Ring is an element of a circular list, or ring. Rings do not have a
    beginning or end; a pointer to any ring element serves as reference to the
    entire ring. Empty rings are represented as nil Ring pointers. The zero
    value for a Ring is a one-element ring with a nil Value.

func New(n int) *Ring
    New creates a ring of n elements.

func (r *Ring) Do(f func(any))
    Do calls function f on each element of the ring, in forward order. The
    behavior of Do is undefined if f changes *r.

func (r *Ring) Len() int
    Len computes the number of elements in ring r. It executes in time
    proportional to the number of elements.

func (r *Ring) Link(s *Ring) *Ring
    Link connects ring r with ring s such that r.Next() becomes s and returns
    the original value for r.Next(). r must not be empty.

    If r and s point to the same ring, linking them removes the elements between
    r and s from the ring. The removed elements form a subring and the result
    is a reference to that subring (if no elements were removed, the result is
    still the original value for r.Next(), and not nil).

    If r and s point to different rings, linking them creates a single ring
    with the elements of s inserted after r. The result points to the element
    following the last element of s after insertion.

func (r *Ring) Move(n int) *Ring
    Move moves n % r.Len() elements backward (n < 0) or forward (n >= 0) in the
    ring and returns that ring element. r must not be empty.

func (r *Ring) Next() *Ring
    Next returns the next ring element. r must not be empty.

func (r *Ring) Prev() *Ring
    Prev returns the previous ring element. r must not be empty.

func (r *Ring) Unlink(n int) *Ring
    Unlink removes n % r.Len() elements from the ring r, starting at r.Next().
    If n % r.Len() == 0, r remains unchanged. The result is the removed subring.
    r must not be empty.
